title: 🏛️ Exams 2005–2019 · writing prepared: letters and e-mails ⭐⭐⭐

questions.prompt: (Exam 2019, technical) Task: "Because of the high cost of water and electricity, you have decided to write an 8-line letter to your friend Asma, in which you give her tips on how to save water and energy at home." The frame starts with "Dear Asma," and ends with "Yours," and "Wahid / Wahida". What is the aim of the letter?

options.text: To complain to Asma about the prices of water and electricity.
To ask Asma for money to pay the bills.
To give Asma tips on saving water and energy at home.
To describe the house where you live to Asma.

questions.explanation: The verb of the task is "give tips": the letter advises Asma on what to do. The high cost is only the reason for writing. Complaining, asking for money and describing a house are different aims, and none of them helps Asma save water or energy.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2019, technical) In the same letter to Asma, which tips are sound?

options.text: Turn off the tap while you brush your teeth.
Leave the tap running so that the pipes stay warm.
Switch off the lights when you leave a room.
Wash the dishes under running water.
Leave the charger plugged in when the phone is full.
Open the windows wide when the heating is on.

questions.explanation: A tip must really save water or energy: closing the tap while brushing and switching off the light in an empty room. The other points waste water or energy: a running tap, dishes washed under running water, a charger left plugged in, and heating that escapes through open windows.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2018, technical) Your penfriend sent you a letter describing his sports school. You write back to talk about the subjects you study and the equipment in your technical school. Which sentence is the best opening of your answer?

options.text: I am writing to complain about the food and the long queues in my school.
Please tell me how much your school costs and how many pupils it has.
Dear teacher, I would like to apply for a place in your sports school.
Thank you for your letter. I was glad to read about your sports school.

questions.explanation: A reply to a friend starts by thanking him for his letter and reacting to what he wrote, before the writer moves on to his own school. A complaint about food, a question about prices and an application for a place speak about other things, and an application is not written to a penfriend.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2013, technical) You write to a friend in the 7th form to advise him to study in your technical school. The hints say "You should / I advise you to". Which sentence is correct and fits the task?

options.text: You should to join our school because it has large workshops.
You should join our school because it has large workshops.
You should joining our school because it has large workshops.
I advise you join our school because it has large workshops.

questions.explanation: After the modal "should" the verb stays in its base form, and the reason with "because" supports the advice. "should to" adds a "to" the modal does not take, "should joining" puts an -ing form after a modal, and "I advise you" needs "to" before the verb.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2012, general) Your English friend Ken wants to know the best way to get from the airport to your town. The hints are the qualities of a means of transport. Match each quality with the means of transport that has it.

options.text: cheap
comfortable
good for long distances
allows sightseeing
the train, which crosses the whole country
the public bus, with a one-dinar ticket
a hired car that stops wherever you like
a taxi with soft seats and air conditioning

questions.explanation: The public bus has the cheapest ticket. A taxi with soft seats and air conditioning is the most comfortable way. The train crosses the whole country, so it is good for long distances. A hired car can stop at any place on the road, so it allows sightseeing.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2012, general) In your e-mail to Ken you compare two means of transport and give your conclusion. Which sentence does it correctly?

options.text: A taxi is more faster than a bus, but a bus is cheaper, so I advise you to take the bus.
A taxi is the fastest than a bus, but a bus is cheaper, so I advise you to take the bus.
A taxi is faster than a bus, but a bus is cheaper, so I advise you to take the bus.
A taxi is faster than a bus, but a bus is cheaper, so you must not take the bus.

questions.explanation: A short adjective makes its comparative with -er and "than": "faster than". The conclusion has to follow from the comparison: the bus is cheaper, so the advice is to take it. "more faster" marks the comparison twice, "the fastest than" mixes the superlative with "than", and the last sentence advises against the cheaper means without any reason.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2011, general) Your English penfriend Tom told you about English teenagers' leisure activities and asks how Tunisian teenagers spend their free time. What must your letter describe?

options.text: Only your own favourite hobbies, with no other teenagers.
The leisure activities of English teenagers again.
The school subjects Tunisian teenagers study.
The leisure activities of Tunisian teenagers in general.

questions.explanation: Tom asks about Tunisian teenagers and their free time, so the letter describes what they usually do: sports, reading, surfing the net, going out with friends. One person's hobbies are too narrow, English teenagers are what Tom already wrote about, and school subjects are not free-time activities.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2010, technical) Linda White, an English pupil, asks for an e-mail "about yourself and your school (name / age / school / practical skills / favourite subjects and future job)". Put these parts of your e-mail in the order of a clear message.

options.text: My school is Modern Technical School, where I learn practical skills.
Thank you for your message. I am glad to write to you.
My name is Sami and I am fifteen years old.
My favourite subject is electricity and I want to become an electrician.

questions.explanation: The e-mail begins with thanks, then follows the order of the questions: name and age, then school and practical skills, then favourite subjects and future job.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2010, technical) In the task the e-mail is sent "from Sami(a)@gmail.com" and "Your name is Sami / Samia". What do you use to speak about yourself in the e-mail?

options.text: Sami if you are a boy, or Samia if you are a girl.
Your own first name and your family name, as on your ID card.
The name of your school and the town where it is.
No name at all, so that Linda cannot know who is writing.

questions.explanation: The task gives the name to use, Sami for a boy and Samia for a girl, so that the paper stays anonymous. Your own name would identify you, the school name is not a person, and leaving out any name would make the e-mail impersonal.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2007) You are the editor of a school magazine. A reader writes: "My parents are very pleased, but I'm worried about my relationship with my friends." and asks: "What shall I do?" Which piece of advice answers the problem?

options.text: You should stop reading and surfing the net for ever.
You should see your friends more, for example in a club.
You must leave your parents and live with your friends.
You should not worry, because friends are never important.

questions.explanation: The reader's problem is the relation with friends, so good advice suggests a way to see them more without giving up what he likes. Stopping reading for ever is too extreme, leaving the parents is not a solution, and saying that friends do not matter ignores the question.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2005) Peter has moved from the country to a big town and writes to Tony to complain about life in town. The hints are "noisy, polluted, too many people, too many cars, no friends, expensive". Which sentence links two of the hints in a complaint?

options.text: I like the town because it is quiet and clean.
The town is noisy, so there are too many cars.
The town is noisy because there are too many cars.
The town is noisy because everything in it is so expensive.

questions.explanation: A complaint states a bad feature and gives its cause: the cars make the town noisy and polluted, and "because" introduces the cause. Saying that the town is quiet is the opposite of a complaint, "so" would make the noise the cause of the cars, and being expensive does not cause noise.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2009, general) You write to your pen-friend, a heavy smoker, to warn him against the dangers of smoking. The exam says: "DO NOT WRITE YOUR NAME OR SIGN THE LETTER." The frame starts with "Dear Chris(tine)" and ends with "Your friend" and "Karim(a)". How do you end the letter?

options.text: Your friend, Karim(a)
Yours faithfully, Mr Karim Ben Salah
With my best regards, the Headmaster
No closing formula: the letter stops after the advice.

questions.explanation: The letter is to a friend, so the printed friendly formula is used with the name given by the frame, Karim or Karima, and not your own name. "Yours faithfully" belongs to formal letters, a signature with a real name breaks the rule of the exam, and a letter with no ending does not respect the frame.
